title: Cavalieri's Principle Demonstration
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: High School Geometry
description: Compare a right solid with an oblique solid that has the same base and height, move a cutting plane through both, and see why their volumes are equal.

educational.topic: Cavalieri's Principle and the volume of oblique solids
learningObjectives: Students will be able to explain Cavalieri's Principle by comparing right and oblique solids with identical cross-sections, and justify why their volumes are equal.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Learner-controlled comparison of two solids with a concrete stack-of-slices model
keyQuestions: What stays the same when the stack is pushed sideways?
Which height matters for an oblique solid, the slanted edge or the vertical height?
Would the principle still hold if the slices had different shapes but equal areas?
commonMisconceptions: A slanted solid has a larger volume because its edges are longer.
The height of an oblique solid is measured along its slanted edge.
Cavalieri's Principle applies only to prisms.
assessmentOpportunities: Students are shown an oblique cylinder with radius 4 cm and vertical height 10 cm and asked for its volume, with a justification that names Cavalieri's Principle and states what must be equal at every height.
